Very enthusiastic team, excited about creating real life solutions with the NASA data
We expect to contribute something usefull and have fun in the process!

Do the impossible, see the invisible
summary: ASTRAL is a 3D atlas of Earth, the Moon and Mars, built from NASA data. Each globe can switch between surface layers: visible color, topography with an elevation legend, shaded relief with adjustable vertical exaggeration, base suitability, and feature names from the IAU and Natural Earth. Click any point on one world and it finds its terrain twins on the other two. Our own neural network, a ResNet-18 trained with self-supervised learning on NASA elevation data (LOLA, MOLA, SRTM), compares landform shape across planets, while a planet discriminator forces it to ignore which world a patch comes from. Six more dimensions measured from NASA data (operations, temperature, albedo, ice, soil and aridity) rank the matches for each mission. Gravity, pressure and radiation are shown with sourced numbers to mark where each analogy stops. Validated blindly, the network places El Pinacate, never seen in training, far above a terrain formula, and links Olympus Mons to Mauna Loa (rank 1 of 7,669). Anyone can try it, and even find their home’s twin on Mars.
details:
What it does. ASTRAL is a 3D atlas of Earth, the Moon and Mars. Click any point on one world and it finds its terrain twins on the other two. Base-suitability layers highlight promising zones at the lunar south pole and on Mars, and “Find Earth analogs” shows where on Earth each site could be studied and rehearsed.

How it works. Our own neural network, a ResNet-18 trained with self-supervised learning on NASA elevation data (LOLA, MOLA, SRTM), turns each terrain patch into a fingerprint. A planet discriminator forces it to compare shape, not planet. Six more dimensions measured from NASA data (operations, temperature, albedo, ice, soil and aridity) explain and re-rank each match by mission. In a blind test it ranked El Pinacate, hidden from training, far above a terrain formula, and it links Olympus Mons to Mauna Loa (rank 1 of 7,669).

Impact. Analog sites are still chosen mostly by expert eye. ASTRAL makes the search global, quantitative and explainable. It proposes new candidates and states where each analogy breaks down (gravity, pressure, radiation), helping teams choose where to train and test before flying.

Creativity. A “planetary Shazam” between three worlds, a 3D map of what the network learned, and “Find your planetary twin” for anyone.

Factors considered. Equal-area scale across bodies, gravity-scaled windows, promising-zone masks, blind validation and honest limits.

Tools. Python (PyTorch, FAISS, GDAL), FastAPI, React, Three.js and GitHub Pages, trained on an NVIDIA RTX 3060.
